title: Regularized glioma expression score associates with survival across archived cohorts
summary: A stepwise-Cox plus ridge model constructed from a supplied glioma expression signature was associated with survival across nine archived cohorts. The final model was selected using average validation-cohort performance, so those cohorts do not provide an untouched external test. The narrow result is a retrospective score–outcome association, not a verified treatment target or clinical-benefit claim.
ai_technology: Mime; stepwise Cox selection; ridge-regularized survival learning

source_review.scope: Exact primary front and selected computational/clinical Methods and corresponding high-level Results; operational laboratory protocols excluded from review

evidence.tested: Mime compared 117 combinations across one development and eight additional glioma cohorts. The selected STRICOM score separated survival outcomes using cohort median scores, and adjusted analyses considered established clinical/molecular covariates.
evidence.unknown: All additional cohorts informed final model selection and model-ranking comparisons; performance can be optimistic. Risk cutoffs are cohort-specific. Input signatures and clinical cohorts are reused, not new randomized or prospective evidence. The SDC1 example includes previously reported biology and is not represented as a newly discovered causal mechanism. Operational perturbation procedures and supplementary experimental details were not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A fitted ridge survival model following feature selection supplies the patient score whose observed survival association is assessed; software availability and visualization alone are not the represented result.
